default.title: How should I use the settings?
default.description: Below each field is the short result of the current selection. By opening the impact and example section, you can examine what the system will do, which operations it will affect, and the real usage scenario.
checklist: Identify which new records and operations this setting will affect.
Confirm that all linked definitions and required fields are ready.
Create one small test operation and verify the result before using the setting in production.

goodsReceipt.title: Goods receipt settings guide
goodsReceipt.description: The current result of each parameter; Examine it along with its impact on order quantity, stock availability, quality gate and ERP receipt. Open orders preserve the rule view at the time of setting.
checklist: Test one purchase-order receipt and one orderless receipt separately.
Confirm that quality-controlled stock and the ERP purchase delivery-note timing work together correctly.
Remember that open work orders may keep their existing rule snapshot, while new documents use the new setting.

inbound.title: Warehouse inbound settings guide
inbound.description: Shows how the selection changes the input quantity, approval gates, quality waiting, shelving and ERP transfer on a field basis and with an example scenario.
checklist: Test separate inbound examples for serialized, lot-controlled, and untracked stock.
Confirm that quality hold, target warehouse/location, and ERP posting rules are ready.
After completion, verify that stock, location, and serial balances are created with the expected status.

outbound.title: Warehouse outbound settings guide
outbound.description: Effects on order source, reservation, under- or over-picking, packing, loading and ERP transfer; Explains with blocking and exception conditions.
checklist: Test full, short, and excess-quantity outbound examples separately.
Verify source location, serial/lot, and available-balance controls.
After completion, confirm that stock, location, serial balances, and the ERP record decrease together.

shipping.title: Shipment settings guide
shipping.description: Explains the result of each selection, from the beginning with or without an order to reservation, barcoded picking, packaging, loading confirmation and ERP dispatch record.
checklist: Test sales-order and orderless shipment flows separately.
Check the sequence of reservation, picking, packing, and loading approval.
After shipment completion, verify balance reduction and the timing of the ERP shipment record.

transfer.title: Inter-warehouse transfer settings guide
transfer.description: Reservation, source issue, transit stock, target acceptance, shelving and quantity difference behavior; Explains with one- or two-step transfer scenarios.
checklist: Test one-step and two-step transfers with different warehouse/location pairs.
Check source issue, in-transit stock, destination receipt, and putaway statuses in order.
Verify that serial and lot values stay unchanged while only warehouse and location change.

quality.title: Quality settings guide
quality.description: Explain with examples the impact of control type, failed quality result, quarantine shelves, stock release, and ERP waiting gate.
checklist: Create separate examples for passed, pending, and failed quality results.
Confirm the quarantine location, stock availability, and ERP quality gate.
For a failed result, verify that stock is not lost and the mandatory receipt-document process continues at the correct time.

packing.title: Packing settings guide
packing.description: Explains package obligation, mixed content, batch and lot verification, SSCC, weighing tolerance, close, reopen and label behavior with examples.
checklist: Test serialized, lot-controlled, and mixed-content packages separately.
Check package closing, reopening, SSCC, and label rules.
Do not enable the setting in production until package content exactly matches stock and serial quantities.

project.title: General project settings guide
project.description: Format settings only change the display; It shows how security, time zone, and ERP serialization choices affect transaction and integration behavior.
checklist: Verify number, date, time, and time-zone examples for all user profiles.
Identify which integrations are affected by ERP serial posting and security options.
Test display-only settings separately from settings that change operation behavior.

subcontracting.title: Subcontracting transfer settings guide
subcontracting.description: Explains the outcome of each rule, from order and supplier binding to partial entry or exit, from quality and approval gates to excess return tolerance.
checklist: Test subcontracting issue and return flows with partial and full quantities.
Confirm supplier, source document, quality, and ERP rules.
Verify the open quantity between issue and return and the excess-return tolerance.

production.title: Production transfer settings guide
production.description: Explains work order source, stock availability, barcoded picking, task and shelf obligation, partial or overdelivery, second step approval and cancellation refund with real scenarios.
checklist: Test ERP work-order, WMS work-order, and unplanned production sources separately.
Check barcode picking, destination staging location, and second transfer approval.
After a short approval, verify that a new work order is created only for the remaining quantity.

kkd.title: PPE process settings guide
kkd.description: Shows the effects of order channel, rights excess, manager approval, personnel connection and future date rules on distribution, warehouse issue and audit records.
checklist: Create entitlement, over-entitlement, and manager-approved distribution examples.
Confirm employee, customer account, stock/group, and period rule matches.
After distribution, verify entitlement consumption, warehouse issue, and ERP result in the same document chain.

procurement.title: Procurement policy guide
procurement.description: Explains with examples how each selection changes the requisition, RFP, supplier quote, revision, supplier portal, and purchase order chain.
checklist: Test requests for quotation with one supplier and multiple suppliers separately.
Confirm that portal, email, price/revision, and approval rules match user permissions.
Verify the complete request ? RFQ ? quote ? purchase-order link and audit record.

barcode.title: Barcode policy settings guide
barcode.description: Indicates in which operation each profile card is used. Segments are combined sequentially; If mandatory data is missing, production is blocked, the sequence segment generates the unique value atomic.
checklist: Create at least one preview and one real barcode for every profile.
Check required fields, separator, transformation, and sequence segments.
Repeat a request with the same idempotency key and verify that a second barcode is not generated.

barcodeProfile.title: How should I edit the barcode profile?
barcodeProfile.description: Each change instantly updates the description and sample barcode behavior. The parts are listed from top to bottom; A single barcode value is created by combining the prefix and brackets.
checklist: Inspect the sample barcode one segment at a time.
Verify that an empty required segment blocks generation and an empty optional segment is skipped.
Confirm that only one sequence segment exists and preview does not consume a real sequence number.

WithinTolerance.summary: Over-acceptance can only be made within the defined percentage limit.
WithinTolerance.effect: The open amount may be exceeded by the tolerance percentage; more are blocked.
WithinTolerance.scenario: 100 AD orders and 5% tolerance, maximum 105 ADs are accepted.
WithinTolerance.decision: This option controls these operations: Accepting ordered goods, Excessive acceptance tolerance. Choose it when you want this result: “Over-acceptance can only be made within the defined percentage limit.”

ApprovalRequired.summary: Excess amount is recorded but the process does not proceed without authorized approval.
ApprovalRequired.effect: Exceeding amount is marked as an exception awaiting approval.
ApprovalRequired.scenario: If 108 AD is received for a 100 AD order, registration will be opened; It is completed after the approval of the supervisor.
ApprovalRequired.decision: This option controls these operations: Goods acceptance approval queue, ERP transfer port. Choose it when you want this result: “Excess amount is recorded but the process does not proceed without authorized approval.”

Immediate.summary: The accepted stock is transferred to the available balance without waiting.
Immediate.effect: Stock; It is immediately opened for transfer, dispatch and reservation transactions.
Immediate.scenario: 10 AD can be selected in another transfer order as soon as the acceptance ends.
Immediate.decision: This option controls these operations: Warehouse and shelf balance, Reservation, Shipment/transfer. Choose it when you want this result: “The accepted stock is transferred to the available balance without waiting.”

AfterReceiptApproval.summary: The stock remains blocked until the goods acceptance approval is given.
AfterReceiptApproval.effect: Physical registration is created, but the available balance is opened after confirmation.

AfterQualityApproval.summary: Stock included in the quality plan cannot be used until the quality decision is made.

AfterAllApprovals.summary: Goods acceptance, quality and all necessary ERP approvals are expected.

AfterReceipt.summary: Once the goods acceptance is completed, the ERP delivery note is ready to be sent.
AfterReceipt.effect: If there is no other approval gate, the ERP queue is triggered immediately.
AfterReceipt.scenario: When the acceptance that does not require quality is completed, a Netsis receipt is created.
AfterReceipt.decision: This option controls these operations: Goods acceptance completion, ERP receipt. Choose it when you want this result: “Once the goods acceptance is completed, the ERP delivery note is ready to be sent.”

AfterReceiptApproval.summary: For ERP registration, the approval of the goods acceptance manager is awaited.
AfterReceiptApproval.effect: Operator completion alone does not initiate ERP transfer.

AfterQualityApproval.summary: In acceptance with a quality plan, the ERP record is not made until the quality decision is completed.

AfterAllApprovals.summary: ERP transfer is made after all defined approvals are completed.

None.summary: The quality plan does not hold up ERP transfer.

RuleBasedOnly.summary: Only inspections arising from the stock/quality rule will hold the ERP transfer.

AnyQualityPlan.summary: Every quality plan opened based on rules or manually will hold the ERP transfer.
AnyQualityPlan.effect: The receipt will not be queued until the quality decision is completed.
AnyQualityPlan.scenario: If the operator manually sends the suspicious product to quality, the delivery note will not be discarded until the quality result is received.
AnyQualityPlan.decision: This option controls these operations: Manual quality plan, Rules-based quality, ERP transfer. Choose it when you want this result: “Every quality plan opened based on rules or manually will hold the ERP transfer.”
